newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia says no privatisation voucher extension.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia says no privatisation voucher extension.

text.p: Slovenia's Ministry of Economic Relations and Development said on Wednesday citizens would have to spend their privatisation vouchers by the end of June this year.
"We will not prolong the validity of vouchers beyond the current expiry date of June 30," Edo Pirkmajer, state secretary for privatisation, told a news conference.

Under a far-reaching privatisation scheme that started at the beginning of 1994, every Slovenian received a voucher with a value of between 100,000 tolars ($640) for people under 18 and 400,000 tolars for people over 48.
To date, citizens have spent 86.6 percent of all vouchers by placing them with Slovenian investment funds or buying shares directly.
Due to the slow pace of privatisation, partly caused by revisions in the valuation of state companies, the vouchers' validity has already been extended four times.
The privatisation involves about 1,500 companies. So far some 950 companies have completed the scheme.

The bulk of privatisations should be finished by the end of 1997 or the beginning of 1998. Investment funds can exchange the collected privatisation vouchers for shares of companies only after sell-offs to employees and citizens are finished. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
